chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah loves kindness and assists upon it. So when you ride the lean animals, dismount them in their resting places. If the land is barren, hasten from it, and if it is fertile, dismount them in their places.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on treating lean animals with kindness?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith links the general virtue of الرفق (gentleness) to practical animal husbandry, illustrating how divine love for kindness translates into specific care for livestock based on environmental conditions. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing compassion with practical wisdom, urging riders to ease the burden on lean animals by allowing them to rest in their natural habitats rather than forcing them through arid or fertile lands indiscriminately.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Loves the kindness and He<sup>azwj</sup> Assists upon it. So whenever you ride the lean animals, so rest them in their places. So if it was a barren land, hasten from it, and if it was fertile, so rest them in its places’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Allah, certainly, loves kindheartedness and He supports one to achieve it. If you ride a weak animal allow it to rest whenever needed. If it is a barren land pass it quickly, and if it is a fertile land, allow them to rest as they need.’”
